description.value: Howard Horel Nature Reserve is a 25-hectare protected area on Salt Spring Island within the globally rare Coastal Douglas-fir zone, featuring forested terrain, rocky bluffs, Garry oak, small wetlands, and streams flowing into upper Fulford Creek. The reserve harbours seven Species at Risk and was acquired in 2018 through an anonymous donation honouring a long-time Salt Spring family. Touring cyclists can access the reserve's easy trail network via Bryant Hill Park, reached from the end of Mereside Road or Sarah Way.

address.value: 265 Blackburn Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2B8

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms this is an active 25-hectare public nature reserve on Salt Spring Island operated by the Salt Spring Island Conservancy, with walking trails described as 'an easy ramble along grassy old roads.' No cycling-specific infrastructure (bike parking, water, washrooms) is mentioned anywhere on the reserve page or subpages — these facilities appear absent from the reserve itself, though the operator's office contact details are clearly listed. The OSM community tag says 'Sidney' but the reserve and its operator are on Salt Spring Island, which is a geographic discrepancy.
concerns: OSM community tag is 'Sidney' but the reserve and its operator are located on Salt Spring Island — possible mis-assignment in the community field.
Address and phone populated from the operator's office (Salt Spring Island Conservancy, 265 Blackburn Road) — these are not the reserve's own coordinates or a visitor facility address.
No bike parking, washrooms, or potable water mentioned anywhere on the reserve page; reserve may lack visitor infrastructure entirely.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The reserve is a legitimate public attraction with easy walking trails that a touring cyclist might visit, but none of the three required WWC criteria (bike parking, water refill, washrooms) can be confirmed from the website or OSM tags. A site visit or direct inquiry with the Salt Spring Island Conservancy is needed to determine whether any facilities exist at the trailhead.
enrichment_extras.notes: Trail access is via Bryant Hill Park, entered from the end of Mereside Road or Sarah Way. Dogs are permitted on leash. The reserve has no admission fee based on the website content.

wow_evidence: 25-ha Coastal Douglas-fir reserve with species at risk; no trail access described.
